scope: Source review of the mapped existing cluster JUnits and archived runtime evidence under the current exception-at-I/O model. It does not exclude other fault models, tests, or concurrent schedules not observed here.

cases.selected_target: ObserverMaster.removeProposedPacket(long): nonempty proposal queue head zxid differs from committed zxid
cases.runtime_identity_required: One named zk1 ObserverMaster object and lifecycle epoch, plus zxid-matched PROPOSAL and COMMIT packets on its follower's physical receive stream. A later check on a restarted instance or another zxid is insufficient.
source_facts: ObserverMasterTest.java:79-109 runs an existing parameterized observer cluster test. Only the true variant enables observer-master ports; its workload issues create, sync, setData and reads. The longer testInOrderCommits at lines 213-258 uses 10001 asynchronous writes from each of two clients.
Follower.java:182-207 handles PROPOSAL by fzk.logRequest then om.proposalReceived, and COMMIT by fzk.commit then om.proposalCommitted, in packet order on the follower thread.

ObserverMaster.java:363-377 appends proposals and checks/removes the queue head; lines 407-418 invoke removeProposedPacket directly from proposalCommitted, with no I/O between those two ObserverMaster operations.
FollowerZooKeeperServer.java:82-115 enqueues proposal logging and commits by pending transaction zxid; a mismatched pending transaction requests process exit, not a locally caught I/O continuation.

The archived healthy path has named quorum packet edges into the exact guard; its 13 eligible doors are quorum readRecord/writeRecord. A read exception leaves Follower.followLeader through its outer catch; a sender write exception closes LearnerHandler's socket. No tested caught door selectively omits one proposal while the same ObserverMaster processes its COMMIT.

cases.selected_target: QuorumPeer.loadDataBase: if (currentTmp.exists()) at pristine line 1169; selected throw is the else IOException at line 1174
cases.runtime_identity_required: The same restarting zk0 QuorumPeer, lifecycle epoch 2, loadDataBase occurrence and JVM thread. Checks in another peer, epoch or startup attempt do not retain the injected fault.
source_facts: CurrentEpochWriteFailureTest.java:57-93 writes stale currentEpoch and a valid currentEpoch.tmp, restarts the existing three-peer cluster, and expects the first peer to start; the selected healthy check sees the temp file.

QuorumPeer.java:1151-1169 reads currentEpoch before the outer epochOfZxid > currentEpoch test, which gates the selected currentTmp.exists() check. General IOException from the read goes to the outer catch at lines 1199-1201 and aborts this startup before the selected check; the prior one-fault pilot observed this exact target loss.

A FileNotFoundException at the initial currentEpoch read is locally caught at lines 1153-1163, but sets currentEpoch equal to epochOfZxid. This makes the outer strict-greater comparison false, so even the selected TARGET_CHECK at line 1169 disappears. This is not a target-retaining alternative to the tested IOException.

The selected throw needs currentTmp.exists() to return false after the outer comparison is true. The unchanged test explicitly creates currentEpoch.tmp. An exception injected into a later temp-file read occurs after the selected check and exits the outer catch; it does not make the preexisting temp file absent.

decision: Keep both checks nonterminal. Do not repeat the old packet or currentEpoch-read plans or promote from healthy target reach alone. A future campaign needs a distinct source-backed operand-changing fault, exact named target retention in a bounded pilot, and an oracle that distinguishes an expected test fixture from a newly triggered selected exception.
